pdf_note: rasterised independently by the verifier at 300 dpi

x_axis.note: slope axis of the source plot, which is VERTICAL: pixel ROWS of the grey dashed gridlines at 0 and 40 deg (86.6 px per 10 deg)

y_axis.note: slip axis of the source plot, which is HORIZONTAL: pixel COLUMNS of the grey dashed gridlines at slip 0 and 0.8

marker.identification: manual: black five pointed stars (TREC Nominal Tests, GRC3); seed positions read by eye, then refined by fitting the shape of an isolated star (template from the star at slip 0.2) within 4 px; centre = centre of the circumscribed circle of the star
marker.swap_note: the source plot has slip on x and slope on y; every point px is given as [row, column] so that the output x is slope and the output y is slip; do not use colour refinement with this ordering

meta.source_title: A study demonstrating that using gravitational offset to prepare extraterrestrial mobility missions is misleading (Hu, Li, Rogg, Schepelmann, Chandler, Kamrin, Negrut; Journal of Field Robotics, 2025; author manuscript in NASA NTRS 20250001809)
meta.vehicle: NASA Glenn TREC single wheel rig, VIPER wheel, velocity controlled (VV mode) on level simulant
meta.x_name: traction slope (arctan of drawbar pull over normal load)
meta.comparability_note: Series 'TREC Nominal Tests, GRC3' (black stars, dashed line). 17 stars: at slip 0.1, 0.3, 0.6, 0.7 and 0.8 two stars share a slip value and at 0.4 three stars overlap; all are kept as separate points. Slope here is the traction slope arctan(DBP/N) on level soil (VV mode), so it is an emulated slope. Output x (slope) comes from the vertical axis.
